title: Should You Buy Extended Warranty On A Car? OR ANY Finance Office Products?
summary: A car-buying advice channel gives conditional guidance on when a dealer extended warranty and other finance-office add-ons are worth buying.

assertions.quote: the likelihood of using the extended warranty and filing a warranty claim is going to be a lot higher

verdicts.note: Higher mileage correlates with higher failure rates for wear components, raising the odds a warranty pays off.

assertions.quote: you might be getting your money's worth out of an extended warranty plan especially if you're buying a vehicle
dealerships can make a lot of money on extended warranties sometimes with a profit margin anywhere from 30 to 50 percent

verdicts.note: With margins commonly cited in the 30-50% range, there is real room for buyers to negotiate the add-on price down.

WTAMU cites a roughly 100% average markup on new-vehicle service contracts, and NCLC an 83% average 2012 dealer markup -- margins large enough to suggest room to negotiate down, though neither source directly tests negotiation outcomes.

assertions.quote: a lot of these third-party companies have a very poor reputation when it comes to their customer service

verdicts.note: The same passage flags third-party auto service plans as 'a particular problem' for complaints and refused claims, but gives no satisfaction percentages to compare against manufacturer-backed plans.

assertions.quote: as long as you're buying it before the original warranty expires you can always purchase one later on
they often don't include a lot of expensive items like replacing your tires and replacing your brakes or draining a lot of the important fluids

verdicts.note: Many prepaid plans are weighted toward low-cost inspections and oil changes while excluding pricier wear items, though coverage varies by plan.
